items.readable_text:
Content:
A situation involves exponential decay if some initial amount repeatedly shrinks due to being multiplied by some constant rate.

Content:
For example, suppose that a certain battery had a voltage of [MATH: 4\,\textrm{V}] when it was healthy. Following a sharp impact, the battery's voltage decreased by [MATH: \dfrac12] every day since the day of the impact. What was the voltage of the battery [MATH: 3] days after it was damaged?

Content:
Starting with a voltage of [MATH: 4\,\textrm{V},] we know that this number will halve every day. So after [MATH: 1] day, the voltage (measured in volts) was

Content:
[MATH: {\color{blue}{4\cdot \dfrac 1 2}}.]

Content:
On the second day, this number halved again. So the voltage after [MATH: 2] days was

Content:
[MATH: \left({\color{blue}{4\cdot \dfrac 1 2}}\right)\cdot \dfrac 1 2 = {\color{red}{4\cdot \left(\dfrac 1 2\right)^2}}.]

Content:
After one more day, the number above halves once again. So the voltage after [MATH: 3] days was

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}{4\cdot \left(\dfrac 1 2\right)^2}}\cdot \dfrac 1 2 = {\color{black}{4\cdot \left(\dfrac 1 2\right)^3}}.]

Content:
If we evaluate the above expression, we get:

Content:
[MATH: 4\cdot \left(\dfrac 1 2\right)^3 = 4\cdot \dfrac 1 8 = \dfrac 1 2]

Content:
So after [MATH: 3] days, the voltage reduced to just [MATH: \dfrac 1 2\,\textrm{V}.]

Content:
This is an example of exponential decay. The voltage decreases by [MATH: \dfrac 1 2] over a time interval of [MATH: 1] day, every day. The voltage decays very rapidly, as we can see from the graph below.

sections.normalized_html:
If the mass of the substance reduces by [MATH: \dfrac 1 3] every year, then [MATH: \dfrac 2 3] of its mass remains every year.

Therefore:

  • After [MATH: 1] year, the mass is [MATH: 4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)\,\textrm{kg}.]

  • After [MATH: \color{blue}3] years, the mass is [MATH: 4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)^{\color{blue}3}\,\textrm{kg}.]

  • [MATH: \ldots]

Repeating this pattern, we see that the mass after [MATH: \color{blue}6] years is [MATH: 4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)^{\color{blue}6}\,\textrm{kg}.]

sections.normalized_html:
The number [MATH: 12\%] written as a decimal is [MATH: 0.12.] Therefore, a decrease of [MATH: 12\%] corresponds to multiplication by a factor of

[MATH: 1-0.12 = 0.88.]

Therefore:

  • After [MATH: 1] year, the annual profit was [MATH: 40\,000\cdot (0.88)] dollars.

  • After [MATH: \color{blue}2] years, the annual profit was [MATH: 40\,000\cdot (0.88)^{\color{blue}2}] dollars.

  • After [MATH: \color{blue}3] years, the annual profit was [MATH: 40\,000\cdot (0.88)^{\color{blue}3}] dollars.

  • After [MATH: \color{blue}4] years, the annual profit [MATH: 40\,000\cdot (0.88)^{\color{blue}4}] dollars.

Finally, let's evaluate the last expression:

[MATH: \[math]40\,000\cdot (0.88)^{4} \approx \[/math]23\,988]

Therefore, Carlton's profit reduced to [MATH: \[math]23\,988] after [MATH: 4] years.
